utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. No preliminaries were announced. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, we are. We are calling our ballistic expert, Ms. Zorica Subotic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Ms. Subotic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, will you tell us your full name.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: My name is Zorica Subotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, have you made reports for the Defence of General Mladic relating to incidents in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we display on our screens first of all 1D05496.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because of the numbers, we'll follow this sequence, but later we'll start with another paper. Let me ask you, do you recognise this cover page?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you participate in the writing of this report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: With Mr. Mile Poparic, who is the co-signatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D05497.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, did you participate in the writing of this expert analysis of the use of modified air bombs in the Sarajevo area in 1994 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With whom did you write this paper?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: With Mr. Mile Poparic and Ms. Mirjana Andjelkovic Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us see 1D5498.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, we now have before us the expert report for the Defence of mortar attacks in the Sarajevo area in 1992-1995. Can you identify this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you work on its drafting?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Together with whom?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: With Mr. Mile Poparic, expert for weapons and military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at 1D05906.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have before us a document. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It concerns what?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: We put in some corrections that we believe clarify the document -- in fact, the documents that we produced, and we noticed that these corrections were needed during proofing for this testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you make these corrections and when did you hand them over to the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but perhaps seven or ten days ago. Maybe later. I really don't know. Because we continued working on them and we added more and more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that the corrections were made concerning the use of modified air bombs on the first page.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you also make corrections on other reports that you produced?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We made corrections for all the three documents that my colleagues and I produced and the document that relates to the use of infantry weapons in the area of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Assault weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D05907 is the next document we need. Can we see the next page of this -- the second page of this report? We have to go back to 1D05906. Let's look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see here at the bottom of the page in B/C/S, but I can't see it in English, that picture 82 has been corrected. But I do not see that correction made -- oh, yes, I do see it. Could you explain briefly?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: When analysing this incident and while preparing for this testimony, we noticed that we had analysed in this incident --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: My apologies, but just I know it's going to be a long course of examinations, but just so we could have a clear record as we go. If we're going to be referring to "an incident," if we could at least on the record have some indication of what event we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if there are any corrections, then of course to know what exactly they are corrections to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have heard this, Ms. Subotic. Just tell us briefly what this is about?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the beginning. It's incident G-7. That's how we marked it. It took place on 4 February 1994 in Dobrinja. When in the street of liberators of Sarajevo, in the street, in the play field, this incident happened very close to the street. That's the incident we are discussing. And now we can go back to picture 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the correction?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: The correction is as follows. If you look at this, you will see that we placed these markings back to the site of the incident, and the entire analysis of this incident, unlike the other incidents, was made from the place of firing. We marked the direction of descent from the place of firing instead of doing what we did in the rest of the paper, marking the descent from the place where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is the correction then? In the calculation of what, relating to what?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: There is practically no correction. All the conclusions remain the same. They are what they are. But we just aligned this incident with the remaining ones in the report, marking the direction of descent from the place where the shell landed. And that's the only correction which you can see from the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, what exactly do you mean by "the direction of descent"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the incoming trajectory of the projectile to the site, the bearing of descent. The azimuth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which is therefore the direction of the origin of fire from -- seen from the place where the shell landed. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm confused, because in that direction, of course, first the shell goes up and then descends, so -- but I now better what you mean by that. Then you say "the place of firing," is that a known place or is that a suggested place of firing? Because this Chamber, I think, still has to establish from where a shell was fired. What did you take there as the place of firing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let's clear one thing up. The place of firing is not adopted. It was determined based on material clues. The incoming trajectory was determined based on material clues, and the first analysis was carried out at a certain place because it was more inconvenient. As you can see, there are many markings on this map. It was more convenient to mark it up here. That's how we did the analysis, and then we harmonised the report. We did not adopt any place of firing. The azimuth was determined at some point of the incoming trajectory, and we marked this trajectory at the place of descent because we believed the whole paper, the whole report should be uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. May I invite you to be very precise in your language because a direction of descent is, if I understand you now well, is the direction of origin, because over the trajectory you first rise and then you go down. So it's not only the direction of descent but it's also the direction of moving up, of firing it. But I am very sensitive for trying to understand exactly what the words mean that you're using. May I insist on a very precise use of words. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, may I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if there is anything -- we are not in a debate. You are a witness here. You are examined. If there is something which I said is wrong -- but there is no reason to enter into a debate. I just asked you to use very precise language. And I am aware that your language first is interpreted and especially if it is technical expressions that may now and then cause confusion. Let's leave it to that. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, to the best of your expert knowledge, what you stated in your report, is it accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After making all these corrections that you've made, would you today still write the same report with the same findings?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we please concentrate now on your report regarding mortar attacks on Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 1D5498. Could we see it on the screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this particular report, since the first part is your CV, could we go straight to page 30 in English and 31 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This incident is not in the indictment. The experts have analysed it in our indictment, in schedule G, item 1. It reads: "Sarajevo was exposed to extensive shelling damaging and destroying civilian targets and killing and wounding several civilians." Regarding the date, it says "beginning with or approximately from 28 May 1992." Just for the record, relating to this incident, although it's not in the indictment, the Office of the Prosecutor introduced several pieces of evidence, several exhibits: P06594, that is photo documentation relating to the explosion in this incident in Vase Miskina Street of 27 May 1992; also P03169, the report relating to this incident; and Exhibit P00946, which is medical documentation concerning persons injured in this incident. We therefore believed that the situation being what it is, we have the right to challenge this documentation and we asked our experts to analyse this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are explaining to the Chamber why you are putting questions. Why not - we have -- you have a ruling - ask questions to the witness instead of explaining to the witness or to whomever that you are entitled to ask questions. You are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. In the future then I will just quote the documents the Prosecution entered into evidence based on eight incidents that are not in our indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you need it for the question to the witness, you should tell. If there is no need to tell the witness what documents you want to talk about, then refrain from doing it. It's the witness who is examined. No further marginal matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, just so we're straight, we haven't opposed this one being discussed. It wasn't part of our opposition. It's come up many times during trial. And I just wanted to offer to counsel, because he's referred to a bunch of documents, that we do have the full investigative file assembled if that would assist him. So I just wanted to let him be also aware that we do have the materials for his use, too. It wasn't a part of our objection and we're -- I just -- if we can assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. And we will exactly show that everything is not in the evidence offered by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put questions to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and to the extent that you can meet the request of Mr. Weber, then please --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- consider that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, what did you manage to pin-point as a problem when examining this case, this incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Well, we pin-pointed a number of problems concerning this incident, which made analysis more difficult. First of all, there is no police report from an on-site investigation which was conducted at the time of evacuation. All we have are photographs. Secondly, there is a police report which bears that date and the photographs attached to it were only created after the entire area was cleaned up; thus, we were unable to decide exactly when it was drafted irrespective of the date. It is also specified in the document that it was attached to the file on the 10th of August that day -- that year. Thirdly, the witnesses stated that two shells landed in Vase Miskina Street and exploded, whereas the documents we had at our disposal refers to only one in terms of the traces it left behind. Fourthly, although there is a very detailed record of all injuries involved, there is a serious discrepancy in the police registering 17 people who were killed and the memorial plaque in Vase Miskina Street contains a list of six people, including seven persons who could not be found among those who were killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, let me ask you this: Do we know who attended the on-site investigation? What can you tell from the documents?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Allegedly there were people from the CSB as well as an investigating judge, but no names are specified. Therefore, we don't know who attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you reach your conclusion that there were several explosions rather than one as is referred to in the report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: There was an on-site investigation report created immediately after evacuation, and a number of witnesses also refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There seems to be a problem. We would need to look at some video footage, 1D05918, and Mr. Ivetic will assist us with that. We are interested in the interval from 25 minutes, 16 seconds to 26 minutes, 11 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your microphone is open, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now we need from 14 minutes, 38 seconds until 15 minutes. 14:38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We stopped at 25:13 instead of 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this correction. We'll just continue now from 14:38 until 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you viewed the footage, could you see a crater at the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were reviewing the police documents that are part of the file, were you able to establish all the parameters you needed?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: When we reviewed the photographs and the police report as well as other documents in the file, we could see that in Vase Miskina Street, the same crater we found in the photo documents was there in September 2010 when we went to visit the site itself on Trial Chamber's orders in the Karadzic case. Then we established that the crater does not match the crater we saw a moment ago. We elaborated it in detail in our paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it would be very helpful to know who took this video, when was it taken, what does it depict, the number, 1D5918, I don't find in the list of documents you see -- you provided us with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber is also on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, if we could just add on to that. If we could just ask for the ERN of video, that would assist us in our systems too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is there is that no surrogate sheet for this video uploaded into e-court, Mr. Lukic, if I understand the message of our Registrar well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have ERN number. It's V000-2825-1-A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And now please an answer to the questions put by Judge Fluegge. What's the video, what does it depict, who made it, when was it made?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Maybe I can assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Lukic thinks that -- a bit surprised that Mr. Lukic, who presents it, couldn't give that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was waiting for the translation in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, then please an answer, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This video is taken by Sarajevo police, I think. But we can check with Ms. Subotic and probably Mr. Weber has better ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when was it taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the day of the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is the 4th of February?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which is 27th of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 27th of May, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it 27th or 25th?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 27th, as I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because I see in the report on -- no, perhaps -- okay. Fine. Please proceed. V000-2825-1-A is also not in e-court, as far as Madam Registrar informs me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Surrogate sheet is not in e-court, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that there is a surrogate sheet, but it has not been -- the video is usually handed over on a disk. It's there?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The disks are handed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It's not in e-court yet but it has been now received by Madam Registrar. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just so we have a clear record, the video that is being broadcast is actually a large compilation from the OTP's collection containing videos of many different incidents. I am familiar with the video that Mr. Lukic broadcasted and his representation in terms of -- generally is correct. We do have the original video which we can upload, which might be easier and actually is of better quality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are always grateful if we can get better quality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I leave it to the parties how they could co-operate in such a way that it will become even clearer than it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens first 1D05717.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: It is a record of on-site investigation, signed by Zlatko Medjedovic and Borislav Stankov. It is dated the 27th of May, 1992. It discuss a forensic investigation that was undertaken on the spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we scroll up or down to see the date? Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is in the first line.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the microphone be repositioned? Because we cannot hear the witness when she approaches the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, the second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document itself --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English, yes. In English version, it's in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness Subotic, the document itself doesn't bear a date. It refers in the content to the date of the on-site investigation. When it was drafted, it's unclear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] We would offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're still waiting for some translations, but we actually believe it would be best to just tender the whole file. We're trying to get it uploaded under 65 ter 33168. This document would be a part of that file. If Mr. Lukic could review that, we will release it. And then maybe it's just more economical for the Chamber to have the whole file. The Prosecution will also be using it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any problems in having the whole file available to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I should see the whole file. I don't know what the whole file is since we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not seen -- the whole file is the whole file of the investigation, and you say you have only seen this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know what in this one is. There are several -- there are two, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We reserve a number, and the parties are invited to sit together during the break and find out whether what Mr. Weber is -- has uploaded, whether that is the whole file or something different so that we know at the -- both parties know what will be in evidence if admitted. Madam Registrar, the number to be reserved provisionally for this number, perhaps later to be replaced by a larger file, would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1243, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that number is -- or perhaps we mark it for identification and perhaps later replace the content by another or a larger file. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, how much photo documentation concerning this report did you come across while drafting your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Two. Two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, is it normal and is it lawful to keep two separate photo documentation files under the same number?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Based on the 15 years of experience and based on the laws of my country that I'm familiar with, it would not be lawful or customary. Any document introduced in a file needs to bear its particular number, or it may be attached to it but nevertheless considered a separate document in the register itself. It is not lawful and it is not customary to have two different documents marked with the same number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, can I just get clarification. The question to you, Madam, by Mr. Lukic was: "To the best of your knowledge, is it normal and is it lawful to keep two separate photo documentation files under the same number?" Oh, okay. Sorry, my mistake. I'm clear. Thank you so much. That's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we see P06594, please. [Interpretation] As we can see in the title, we have a photo documentation file compiled by the CSB in Sarajevo, number 1615/29, dated the 27th of May, 1992, discussing the fall and explosion of a mortar shell, 82 millimetres in calibre, in Vase Miskina Street. We are interested in page 6 in B/C/S since the English version does not contain the photograph we are interested in. That page isn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can you see in the photograph, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: We can see the traces of an 82-millimetre shell explosion on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the source of the photograph, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is contained in the second photo documentation file compiled subsequently after the street was cleaned up. And in our view, it is unknown when it was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we now go back to 1D05498, which is your report, Ms. Subotic, discussing mortar attacks in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are interested in page 43 in English and 44 in B/C/S. Can we please enlarge the photograph in the English version of the document, including the caption, so we can all see what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can see it on the screen now. Can you tell us where this photograph comes from?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: We located the source of the photograph. It is on the internet. It was taken by war correspondent Roger Richards during a concert played by Vedran Smajlovic at the site where those people were killed on the Vase Miskina Street. On the photograph, you can clearly see the traces of the shell and its explosion against the pavement. It is exceptionally clear, as a matter of fact. It helped us to compare this photograph against the two existing photo documentation files.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at page 45 in the English and 46 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the comparison here, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: The comparison is between the two craters, one from the photo documentation file that was subsequently created and the crater or the photograph taken by Roger Richards. We rotated the photograph so as to place the craters in an identical position in order to be able to compare. We can clearly and undoubtedly see that these are actually not two same craters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for the photograph in the police file, were you able to identify when it was attached to the file itself?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said a moment ago that there is a handwritten note on the file cover that the photo documentation was attached to the file on the 10th of August, 1992, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps zoom in on the two craters depicted in the two photographs that we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we can do it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- can't see anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we can do it in both languages because they are the same in both. Yes, could we zoom in?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please explain, Ms. Subotic, what is the difference that you can see? And please refer to the left- and right-hand side photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, perhaps we can cut this short. The tiles on the floor are not similar even. So therefore, it's difficult to even imagine that this would be the same because the ones are squares, the other ones are rectangles, where one side is longer than the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It doesn't need a lot of explanation that what is depicted here is not the same. Now, what is what, of course, is the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You heard the reference, Ms. Subotic. It is clear, therefore, that these are not the same craters. Can you tell us which is which?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: I visited the location. I measured the tiles, and they are 40 by 40 centimetres in size. This may have to do with the angle of the photograph, giving an impression that they are not the same tiles. However, it is the same location and we see two comparable craters because on both photographs the craters were reduced to the same dimensions, as you can see, in order to be able to better compare. We can see with the naked eye that these are not one and the same crater. It is also a fact that in Vase Miskina Street the tiles measure 40 by 40 centimetres, because I measured them. However, both photographs were taken in Vase Miskina Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have a question. It looks as if -- to the left, that is the photograph taken by Mr. Rogers, that they are not square. So if you say the tiles there are 40 by 40 centimetres, that at least suggests that perhaps the tiles on the left photograph taken by Mr. Rogers are not in the Vase Miskina Street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the document from which we took this file, it is said the concert was held at Vase Miskina Street on the site of the explosion. Because the musician was a cellist who held 22 concerts in 22 different sites that involved killings and one of them is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all in your report. But the accuracy of what is stated in that book is not within your field of expertise, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While your expertise can assist us greatly, but whether or not something written in a book by a photographer talking about a cello concert, whether that's true or not, and whether you can rely on that I would say is not within your expertise, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at picture number 13 in the report, you will recognise that this was happening in Vase Miskina Street. We don't need to rely on his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you invoked it a second ago. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's break time anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just have couple of more questions so we finish this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that would be suitable for you, for your client, then the Chamber has no problems if Mr. Weber hasn't any. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you visit the site? You said you measured these slabs. When you were on the site?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: On the 17th and 18th of September, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that moment, did the site look the same or was it modified?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: The crater depicted in picture 15 was consistent with the crater as shown in the photo documentation made later, but the appearance of the site was altered because the slabs or the stones covering the street had been changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And were they changed after 2010 in that same place?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes. After my testimony in the Karadzic case, the slabs were changed once again and my colleague, Mr. Poparic, photographed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can have a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes at 11.00. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we invite the witness to enter the courtroom, I see that Mr. Lukic is not present. He's aware that we'll start, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I believe he stayed back to consult about the identification of parts of video-clips he intends to use now in the examination of our experts. In a couple of minutes, we will see if it is ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, not in a couple of minutes. We are already 12 minutes delayed, and Mr. Lukic should come to the courtroom. And then -- I mean, there is sufficient time within the next breaks to deal with any matter he'd like to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Here he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. I don't know what's the decision in regard because it's very hard for us to continue the trial with the help of our expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, a decision on what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Decision on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- his right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me cut this short. I do understand that you sent the Registrar to convey a message that if Mr. Poparic could not be with you in the courtroom that there would be no trial. That's the message we received. That's a message which doesn't require any decision. We are still waiting -- and we were informed that you were given the choice. We are still waiting for your decision, that is, whether you ask permission of an expert to be in the courtroom with you or to decide that you would be satisfied if that expert would follow the proceedings from the public gallery. I do understand that that expert entered those premises as a visitor, not specifically being announced, and moved into areas where visitors are not allowed to come --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not true. Our visitors are allowed to come into this hearing. And message transferred to you is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did not send that message.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But nothing at this moment was submitted to us what requires a decision. Are you intending to ask us something?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please do so, and then we'll see whether a decision will be taken on what you are asking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I asked Registrar to transfer the message that we need our expert to be with us during the breaks here in the courtroom to help us with the documents and the videos. Obviously, the first video we showed was not hundred per cent correct. We saw some church, we didn't have -- we're not supposed to see because we don't need it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What are you asking from this Chamber, Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because then we decide only on --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I was offered that -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we only decide on the requests that are addressed to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I was offered that I can either ask for this gentleman to be with us inside the courtroom helping us or to be in the public gallery. So it's not the question I sent to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But if it's possible, fine. The solution would be if Mr. Poparic can be with us inside the courtroom, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you're asking permission to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that Mr. Poparic is with you in the courtroom. I'll consult with my --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I can add one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He is expert, this is his work as well. And he signed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, that's what we all know, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And he signed undertaking. He has signed undertaking that he cannot disclose anything that is confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have introduced this right from the beginning in saying: One of our next witnesses, Mr. Poparic, is here, and we would like him to be with us in court so that we can consult him on technical matters, he has signed an undertaking, then most of the fuss would have been avoided, I think. But we'll now follow properly procedure. Mr. Weber, is there any objection if Mr. Poparic would be with Mr. Lukic in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The one consideration that the Prosecution wanted to have would just be communication on the witness on the stand. So the witness is under oath and that if the other co-author of the report were to be present communicating with the Defence throughout the course of the examination, we would just ask to make sure that there are some strict provisions that that individual isn't then communicating with the witness during the course of her testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If that's your only concern, then one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided on the matter. Mr. Lukic, the request that Mr. Poparic will be with you in the courtroom is granted. We'll give clear instructions to Mr. Poparic. I add to this that what was reported to us was that you were not very polite to the -- to our court officer. Certainly, it's not acceptable that you sent her as your messenger to the Court. If there is any matter, you can address the Court yourself. If you say: Well, I do not -- I may have been not very nice in my communication with her, then we'll accept that. We understand that as a kind of an apology. If, however, you say: No, that's not true. I behaved properly, appropriately, and never in any way unpleasant to the Registry, then we'll do a further investigation on what exactly happened, what words were used, et cetera. But we are willing to leave it like that if you would agree that, as was reported to us, that your language has not only been pleasant to the court officer. And I use the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can say, Your Honour, that my tone might be angry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- but not words. I never uttered any indecent word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not indecent, but sending her and telling the court officer that if the witness could not be with you that there would be no trial, if the -- these are approximately the words you uttered, then first of all you shouldn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you then say exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I already told you, I never asked for him to be with us. I asked for him to help us during the breaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it cannot be the message that I asked for him to be with us, and that's what -- something I heard from the Registrar, that he can't be with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you used the wrong channel. That was the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should have addressed the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was informed by the guards that I should address the Registrar and solve the problem with him, and that's how I proceeded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you are a lawyer, you know how it works in this courtroom, and you also know that if there is any problem in this respect, that finally, if it's not resolved, that you have to address the Chamber. And let's be quite honest, the way in which we started after this break, there was a lot of agitation in your tone as well. Let's leave it to that and let's try to overcome that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I can say one thing in my defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just tried to solve a problem during the break without involving Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the best -- the best you were doing --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I trying to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The best you are doing now is smiling and relativising apparently what happened. Please be assured, Mr. Lukic, that whenever we have the feeling that our staff is approached in a way even with a tone which is not the appropriate one, that this Chamber will, of course, be very vigilant to see that this does not occur again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's clear to you, then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And just one word of advice, Mr. Lukic. Don't take guidance from the guards. You use your professional knowledge of how to handle matters in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which does not mean that you can ignore what guards say. I mean, if they stop someone, that should be respected. Let that be also clear. But whom to address to resolve the problem, I think your first compass should be your own professional knowledge and skills. We leave it to that. Mr. Poparic can enter the courtroom. The Chamber has now given permission to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will send our colleague to tell Mr. Poparic that he can be with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And since I would like to instruct Mr. Poparic not in the presence of the witness, I hope that he arrives soon. Mr. Mladic is talking aloud which he is supposed not to do. Mr. Lukic, while we are waiting for Mr. Poparic to enter the courtroom, there is a risk that after having consulted with Mr. Poparic, that you would lead the witness, so we'll be very strict. If you have someone assisting you in the courtroom and to consult you on technical matters, please be aware that especially under those circumstances, that leading questions are even more strictly prohibited, I would say, than they are already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, there was a short discussion in this courtroom about your presence. That matter has been resolved. You are allowed to sit in the courtroom so that Mr. Lukic can consult you if he wishes to do so. At the same time, I have to give you clear instructions as well; that is, that you refrain from any intervention with the examination of the witness, whether that's eye contact, whether that is anything else, nodding yes or nodding no, whatever it is, you should refrain from it, rather not even look at the witness. That's one. Second, as long as this witness has not concluded her testimony, you are not allowed to communicate with her in any way in relation to her testimony. That should be perfectly clear to you. And this is an order by the Court, which means that if you would violate that order, you can be prosecuted for that. So you should refrain from any communication in relation to the testimony. Now, the best way to do it is to avoid contact anyhow with this witness, because otherwise people might think that you are communicating. And so that's -- whether it's by telephone, whether it's by -- through e-mail, nothing. You have to refrain from everything. You are here so as to allow the Defence to consult you. Is that clear to you? Perhaps if you switch on the microphone, if you say -- if you answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPARIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then with these restrictions, you are -- you may be seated again. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam, the break took a bit longer than expected. One of the things you may notice or have noticed already is that Mr. Poparic is here in the courtroom as well. You are hereby instructed to avoid any communication, eye contact, whatever. He's here to be consulted by the Defence, and he should stay out, and you should also not seek in any way any contact with him. Further, if you leave this courtroom today, I will give you further instructions that you are not allowed to speak or communicate in any way with whomever about your testimony. That is especially valid for any communication with Mr. Poparic. So no discussions, nothing. Best would even be to avoid contact with him up till the moment that you have concluded your testimony. I'll give you the instruction at the end of this session to remind you of that. Mr. Lukic will now continue his examination. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have on our screen -- oh, we have the document we need. I just need picture 17. It's in English version page 48, and in B/C/S version page 49.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have told us that the square slabs are shown here, but I want to ask you something else about the place of detonation. Did you have an opportunity, Ms. Subotic, to determine approximately from which distance from the place of detonation this bomb was fired?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Based on the technical specifications of the weapon and the description of the impact of shrapnel on the pavement, the shape of the crater which helped us determine the angle of descent, and the fact that the tail fin did not embed itself, instead it was found further away from the scene, we managed to determine a distance of 100 to 120 metres along a direction - that is to say, azimuth - of 75 [as interpreted] degrees, which can also be seen from the photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your view, under whose control this territory was?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: This sector was under the control of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, these are questions without a foundation that shouldn't be asked the witness. I mean, who was in control of what territory is evidence which is not to be provided unless there is a specific basis of knowledge for that. I earlier said let's focus on what this witness is called for, that is, her expertise on the matter. And I have one additional question. You said you calculated that this was the distance, 100 to 120 metres. Where do we find that calculation exactly? I mean, angle of descent and -- I mean, taking from that what charges were used in firing the projectile. Is it -- have you given the details in your report exactly? Firing tables for the weapon used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly. We provided that. It's all given in detail on pages from 31 to page 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I mean the calculation of the 1- to 120 metres. Where exactly is that to be found, so to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not necessary to look for that. This data is contained in the firing tables, and we referred to them. It is cited on page 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just if I can have a kind request. If -- there is some difference in pagination numbers between the English and the B/C/S, but the paragraph numbers are the same. If it's possible to refer to the paragraph numbers, so we could understand in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist with the paragraph number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, it's paragraph 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we have paragraph 16 on the screen. It must be page 52 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And paragraph 15. Paragraph 15 provides an excerpt from the firing table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll look at that later, but I just wondered where to find the exact details. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the video, Ms. Subotic, that we have just seen, were you able to conclude what accompanied the evacuation of the injured?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: We could hear the sound of fire from infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We should now like to play 65 ter 1D05918. It's V000-2825-1-A. And we should see from 30 minutes, 47 seconds to 30 minutes, 49 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I correct that you said it was 100 to 120 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Perhaps we first look at the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out what is written on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Sarajevo, 27 May 1992, Vase Miskina Street, 9.30. And in the upper corner we see BH TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we have no translation, we have to play this same video once again. [In English] Yeah, can we play? I was just informed that it was not played. Can we play it now, please? Those two seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that's the scene we want to see. And now if we can see the same video from 33 minutes, 44 seconds until 34 minutes, 04 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we stop here? Actually, we can continue, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stop. For the record, we stopped at 33 minutes, 51 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, can you read what is written here?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Sniper fire during first aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This place where the incident happened, where is it? Where can you see it from? Who was able to open fire from a sniper rifle or any other rifle?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: That place is found surrounded by high-rise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There is a couple of questions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the place of the incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the place of the incident, the appearance of the surrounding buildings, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: The place of the incident is in a street where there are high-rise buildings on both sides, which you can see on pictures 1 and 2. I repeat: The place of the incident is in a street which has high-rise buildings on both sides, as we can see from pictures 1 and 2. This place is not visible from a great distance and can be targeted only from close proximity, and the sounds that we hear also indicate that the fire is coming from the vicinity. I must say that the closest positions of the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska, are located at 1700 to 1800 metres from this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is your conclusion regarding this incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: As I've said, according to technical parameters that we had at our disposal, this incident could have involved an 82-millimetre calibre shell fired from a distance of 100 to 120 metres from the spot. That is my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you about incident G-4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you would allow me to ask a few follow-up questions. I think the 100 to 120 metres, that's what you said before. You said, and I'm referring to page 13: "... we managed to determine a distance of 100 to 120 metres along a direction - that is to say, azimuth - of 75 degrees ..." Do I understand that this 75 degrees are referring to the compass which is then -- approximately 75 degrees is east of north-east?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There apparently is a problem with the audio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ah, yes. It's okay. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Is it 75 degrees --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now it's okay. Now it's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. 75 degrees, is that the direction of the origin of fire? Is that what you are referring to? The azimuth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The azimuth is 175 degrees, and it's close to the perpendicular line to the pavement, that's the direction of descent. That's the azimuth, 175. It is visible on picture 19, paragraph 14, in our report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there must have been a mistake in the -- perhaps in the transcription. I would like now to take you back to, as you said, on page 50 in the English, and unfortunately I am unable to tell you which page it is in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the name of the -- the number of the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I will give that to you, Mr. Lukic, if you've got one second. I think it is paragraph 15. Paragraph 15, table 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we have it on the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's page 50 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 50 in B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 50, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There we see the table which I asked you about. In paragraph 15 you are explaining that the angle of descent was close to the maximum angle, which is 83 to 84 degrees. Is it true that in the table, you calculated everything on the basis of the maximum angle rather than on any angle close to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We provided data here from the firing table for angles from 83 to 84, which is written there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you said that on the basis of the crater shape, that the angle of descent was close to the maximum angle of 83, 84, so therefore may I take it that it has been less, much or a bit, or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We need to understand that this angle is on the order of 83 to 84, as we wrote. That estimate could be made only at that level. It was close to the maximum possible angle, and we provided data for this value. A little less than that would give a result very close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you have told us that you established that the distance was between 100 and 120 metres. If I look at this table, then I see that the distance the projectile travelled depends on the charges that were used in firing it and that only if fired with a primary charge that the outcome would be close to 120 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to believe that there was only a primary charge used and not, for example, charge 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have very serious technical reasons to conclude that. You wouldn't have the same situation on the pavement as you would have if charge 6 had been used. That's a very well-known specification. The tail fin, beginning with charge 3, embeds itself into the surface, more or less, depending on the quality of the surface; whereas we found the tail fin removed from the place where the shell landed, so it could not have been charge 6 or 5 or 4 or 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you calculated that exactly on the basis of the quality of the surface?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not show that. There is a very simple formula which factors in the quality of the surface, and I stand by this piece of information that charge 3 -- or had charge 3 been used, the tail fin would have been buried in the surface to some extent. Ultimately, if you look at the table results, you will see that even charge 3 is still within ABiH territory. We specified a primary charge because the -- we did not have a single piece of evidence of anyone hearing the firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you limit yourself to metres rather to tell by whom the territory was controlled. That's not within the field of your expertise. If you say that it is at that distance, then that's certainly within your field of expertise. But apparently you took the primary charge only and not charge 1 or charge 2, you did not consider that because you said it was 100 to 120 metres. And for example, for charge 2 it goes already to 625 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I see two numbers. Let's just take as an example charge 2 for an 82-M 68-millimetre mortar shell. We see 384 to 625. Is the one number for 83 and the other one for 84, or what does this range stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 74. These are possible ranges as well. We provided the most probable one, but the other ranges included are also probable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it could be up to 625 metres on charge 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just -- just for argument's sake, let's assume it wasn't 83 or 84 but it was 80 degrees, what difference would that have made in the outcome?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would look at the firing tables before I answer it. I don't know these things off the top of my head. In any case, it wasn't specified here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps, Mr. Lukic, we have some firing tables in evidence. I see that here is -- a reference is made to a certain 65 ter number. Wouldn't it be a good idea so in order to be able to verify the accuracy where the witness at least was selective in choosing the 100 to 120 millimetres, where she now tells us that it could have been fired with charge 2 perhaps as well, and that gives it an entirely different outcome. Although the witness still says within BiH-controlled territory, and, of course, the Chamber will, on the basis of the evidence before it, rather than on what this witness tells us, find out whether it was or was not from within BiH-held territory. Firing tables, perhaps a selection. The relevant selection. We don't need the whole booklet, perhaps, but just for these mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or is it already in evidence? I must say that we have -- for 120-millimetre I think we have them in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour's recollection is accurate. If it assists Mr. Lukic, regarding the three types that are listed here, the Prosecution has uploaded the related firing tables under 65 ter 33098, which I -- are not yet admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Lukic has uploaded them as well. I leave it to you which one is first to tender that, but I'd be interested and the Chamber might be interested in having a look at the tables. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm certain that the Presiding Judge was referring to 100 to 120 metres and not millimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, as a matter of fact I was -- I don't know -- if I was talking about shells I was talking about 120 millimetres. When I was talking about distances, I was talking about 120 metres. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that our 65 ter for these tables are 1D5716, and it's in the footnote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that it's in the footnote, but I wondered whether you wanted to tender that because usually we do not inspect any evidence which is not tendered by a party.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can expect -- inspect it, but I don't know the correct page number where that could be found, even one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would try to find out that and then tender the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: They appear to be the -- the two 65 ter numbers given by both sides appear to be the same original document. If Mr. Lukic could just check the translations in the Prosecution version to verify if those may be more complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And of course apart from exactly 83 and 84 degrees, if other pages deal with different angles of descent, we would like to see what the variety and the angle of descent would mean for the distance over which the projectile has travelled. So therefore, not just limited to 83, 84, but a bit broader. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was just informed by Mr. Poparic that it's not easy. It has to be calculated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this is exactly what you're supposed not to do; that is, to tell in the presence of the witness what Mr. Poparic told you. If there is any question to be put to this witness on the basis of your consultation with Mr. Poparic, then you do not say a word about what Mr. Poparic told you. You just put the question to the witness. Mr. Lukic, this is exactly what is inappropriate to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. What I wanted to ask Your Honours is that somebody provides Ms. Subotic with those tables, because we cannot do that, Mr. Poparic cannot do that. So the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it's in evidence. We can ask the witness -- if you tender it, then of course we can ask the witness to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But maybe she can calculate it at home or overnight or during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's mainly finding the outcome in the tables. If you remember the 120-millimetre tables, you say this angle of this -- as a matter of fact angle of firing or angle of descent, we have to compare how the angle of descent is different. It's usually slightly different from the angle of firing, and then you read in the tables what the distances are if fired with initial -- a primary charge or plus 1, plus 2, up to plus 6. Therefore I have no --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can try but I cannot because I was not prepared for this. We can call 65 ter -- as the Prosecution offered, maybe it is translated, 33098.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then we still have to find the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- pages we need --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, it is in total 301 pages. I thought it's on page 306, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the first thing I see, Mr. Lukic, is that this is about M69 and M69A and not about M68 as well. And it's these three -- as a matter of fact, in the report the outcome are given for 82-millimetre M68, M74 and M72. And what I see on our screen now apparently is a table for projectiles M69 and M69A. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could assist you, maybe if you could go to e-court page 6 where you see the table of contents where that might give an indication as to where to go to the ones you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a look at page 6 then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I was referring to page 6 of the original B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break. And, Mr. Lukic, I take it that during the break you will be able to find exactly the pages which we would --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If Ms. Subotic leaves the courtroom, I can inform you about the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'll ask Ms. Subotic to first leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can leave? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I was just informed that we would probably need 15, 16 pages from this table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. And we will locate them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you locate them then --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we would just appreciate just having a discussion about that because we would ask for more relating to the rest of the charges so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And all three types listed in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So that we find the proper basis, the source of what the report tells us as far as distances are concerned. We take a break and we resume at 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness is with us, I just want to inform you that Mr. Poparic found pages in this 65 ter. And for -- basic for first, second, so if you want me to tell you those pages for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could give the pages. But again, Mr. Lukic, if you consult Mr. Poparic, you just tell us: Judges, please look at those and those pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it comes from Mr. Poparic or from anyone else is not -- you can consult with him but that's not to be put on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. So the pages are 81, 84, 88, 93, 99, and 106.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the sixth one is 114. It's for M74 mine. And for M68 is page 129 for basic, 132 for first, 136 for second, 141 for third, and 147 for the fourth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: M69 is a mortar itself, not a mine. But there are two mines, 68 and 74. 69 is mortar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if you want to add anything. Of course, we are -- I think we are talking about shells fired with various charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll be very quick. I agree with Mr. Lukic's last representation in terms of type of mortar versus types of mortar shells. That being said, I did discuss this with Mr. Lukic during the break. The Prosecution does want additional pages that correspond to our uploaded translation. Ms. Stewart is going to cut it down and then we'll reoffer that, and we'll make sure that the pages indicated by Mr. Lukic are included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. They will certainly be included. There may be more. Is there a way of presenting those pages, if you have finally made up your mind, to send an e-mail to Chamber staff to tell what pages they are and what you intend to upload, and then Mr. Lukic has an opportunity to look at it as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. But I think that we agreed already during the break that I do not have a problem with having more pages translated. They will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll hear -- then you communicate to Mr. Lukic what you need in addition to what he needs, and I think the Chamber has expressed an interest in looking at angles of descent slightly lower and perhaps up to 10 or 20 per cent lower. That's because 83, 84 is one aspect. I don't know how much details there are in those tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, since we are in the presence of the witness, I'll keep this short, but we believe that greater angles than that are relevant. So we are going to include the ones that we think are relevant based on that evidence. There will be further examination then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. We'll then hear from you and we'll see what will be tendered into evidence. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, we will again require your paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is our number 1D05498. We need page 55 in the English and 56 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is about the 1st of June, 1993. As stated here, at around 1000 hours, two mortar shells landed and exploded in a parking-lot behind a building in Vahida Maglajlic Street at the time when a football match was played. In your report, you specify that in this incident many fighters were killed and wounded. Where did you come across that piece of information?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: In the security services' report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we next on our screens have 1D00693.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm informed by Madam Registrar that opening the English translation into e-court turns out to be impossible. Could you please check carefully whether everything has been uploaded and released.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I anticipated the problem and I already told my colleague to check it, although there is English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's apparently not accessible at this moment. Could you check?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We continue with B/C/S version for now. I'll read the first page and we only need one paragraph or two from the second page -- or we should wait?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should release the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it has to be done from another room, so we just sent a message.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If it's a limited portion and if you take care that it will be released as soon as possible, we have a look at the B/C/S version while you slowly read anything that you need to ask a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read -- we can open it in e-court. It's not released, I was just told. Okay. I will read what we can find on the first page -- and it's released now. [Interpretation] We can see that it comes from the security administration of the Supreme Command staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The date is 6 June 1993. It is a special report. Next, we need page 2 in both versions of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we look at the first paragraph, is this where found the information about the incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is stated that seven fighters were killed and 51 wounded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It also specifies that a warning had been issued - that is the next paragraph - concerning the danger of shelling, but the participants obviously did not heed the warning.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is also stated that the military security services engaged in identifying the initiator and organiser of the tournament.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have a police report about the incident at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: No. Although we know that it exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you did not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'll intervene at this moment. This witness is called as an expert witness, not to interpret other documents to tell us how many fighters were killed. There is no problem in presenting that evidence, but this witness is not qualified to bring any of that to us.
