I think that even such reports might -- you might even be able to tender them by other means, but this witness is here because she is an expert on shelling and she's not an expert on who is a fighter, who is not a fighter, whether this is an authenticate document, et cetera, et cetera. Again, I'm not barring you from presenting that evidence. It may be very important to the extent it is not yet there. I have a vague recollection that there was some evidence about fighters among those who were victims of that shelling incident, so to that extent it would also be repetitious. But this witness is not here to tell us these kind of things. This witness is not here to tell us whether a memorial gives different names, and if so, this the witness should limit herself to say: I saw these names here, I saw these names there. She is not in a position to draw conclusions from that. She is an expert and we accepted her as an expert on matters within her expertise. Would you please keep that in mind also because you asked for ten more hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you try to find out whether Mr. Weber disagrees that there were men reported as being fighters, whatever that means, but among those who were victims of that incident. You should clearly understand what the role of this witness is and what the kind of evidence you are presenting, because we'll certainly not extend to ten hours by asking a witness about matters which he is not -- has no personal knowledge about and which does not fall within the scope of her expertise. Please keep this in mind when you're using the hours which are available to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, you didn't have your headphones on, and my main focus was on the investigation and what was available to Ms. Subotic, and I asked her, since we here see that security organ of the army was interested in this, and I asked Ms. Subotic whether she had report made by the police. She said "no."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was your second question --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and of course it's totally unclear to this Chamber what sources were available to this witness and not. Apparently, there was a lot of material which is really not linked to her expertise, and I'm drawing your attention to that. I'm not specifically criticising your asking whether she knows whether a police report exists or not. That is closely linked to her own work. But whether these were fighters or not, which seems not to be in dispute that there were such fighters, why bother the witness with that? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But we did not know if something is in dispute or not because nobody informed us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that anything is in dispute. We don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you could ask, isn't it. If you present --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. We are open now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you present --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are open now to hear from the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- if there is anything that is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic. You have an active duty to find out whether you present evidence on matters which are in dispute. If I remember that the Prosecution has presented evidence which includes, if I'm not wrong, that there were fighters among the victims, then you should know as well, and you can verify with Mr. Weber. And again, I said you may proceed. This was not a beginning of a debate with me but just a ruling. And it's not right that you should wait until the Prosecution tells you what they agree on. You should analyse the evidence presented by the Prosecution, which gives you a clue on where the issues in dispute are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll just wait for the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, did the police conduct an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: UNPROFOR reported that they received information from the Dobrinja police. It is contained in their report. They say that the Dobrinja police told them that the police had carried out an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see P644, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I know that we're moving on to a different document, but just so counsel is aware, if he does intend to tender that last document at a later stage, if he could please verify the translations for paragraphs 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you to my learned friend to drawing our attention if there is something incorrect. We have probably confirm it with the CLSS since it's their translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, before us is an investigation report regarding a mortar shelling in Dobrinja and Sarajevo on 1 June 1993. We see that it was prepared by the Canadian forces military police on 7 July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have page 5 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S version. We are interested in paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the Canadian forces' report, we see that they met with Mr. Kosavec and the chief of police, and that they were told that all investigative material relating to this incident had been forwarded to the main police station in Sarajevo. While preparing your report, did you have occasion to see the police report in question?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you read any witness statements concerning the incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a witness statement that you would single out as being characteristic?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: I would single out two witness statements, because they were very helpful in our analysis. The witnesses are Dinko Bakal and Ismet Fazlic. Thanks to their statements and the footage made by the BiH TV, we were able to draw conclusions relating to the incident. We concluded that the match was not played at the parking-lot where the on-site investigation was conducted but actually on a field near the parking-lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 65 ter 09939. It is the same document, although it was my impression that they were two documents, different ones. We need page 57 in the B/C/S and 58 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I was informed that there are four B/C/S translations attached to this problem. What we are looking at now is the first of the B/C/S translations. I've got no idea whether there is any difference or not, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was checked. I was just informed that now it's on page 5 in this version, cut version. In B/C/S. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we are waiting for the next question, Witness, could you tell us how did you select any statements you read and you used to draw conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A selection of the statements was made primarily on the basis of material evidence. We only relied on such statements which fit into the concept of material evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But who made that selection? Did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what was then the range of material that was available to you, accessible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case in particular or generally? You mean this incident?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, this case. The case in which you wrote this report. I mean, if you say: I only use material evidence, I do not know exactly what you mean by that, but perhaps you can explain that later. But what was the -- I would say the totality of materials which you could choose from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of the material we analysed is contained in the witness statements, the footage made by the police and Mr. Hogan, as well as all the analyses and investigations made by the CSB in the field, as well as all UNPROFOR reports from the field concerning the incidents referred to in the report. Also, we visited the locations in person, all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But how did you get -- how did you receive that material? I take it that you don't have it at home, all the witness statements. I mean, who provided that to you, where you then made further selections of what you considered to be material evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Initial material was received when we were drafting our first reports for the Karadzic case. We received it from the Tribunal upon our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would, to some extent, surprise me. Was it by the Defence that you received that, or did you receive it from the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A part of the material was received through Defence, and some of the material was received by my government, which contacted the Tribunal. Within a relatively short period of time we received the material directly from the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is it anywhere described what material exactly you had available when you started or a list of documents or videos or whatever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We only referred to such material that we used, but we did not draw up a separate list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said you only used material evidence. What do you mean by "material evidence"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say I used only material evidence. What I wanted to say is that I relied on such statements and video footage which tallied with the material or physical evidence that existed in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need page 57 in English. Sorry, we have to go one page back. And I cannot locate in B/C/S in this because -- this is different version in B/C/S, so I cannot follow this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read for you from English version, Ms. Subotic. And it's where the text starts, and it -- there is some initials and this is the answer of DB, Dinko Bakal. And I would quote: "I was about 60 to 70 metres away from the place where the shell landed. That happened about 10.25 to 10.30 a.m. I was in the apartment at the first floor, from where I was able to see the playground very well."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want to further read or put a question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I should put a question. I would rather actually have video now shown to everybody, with the help of Mr. Ivetic. And it is 1D05919. It is ERN number V000-3497.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Lukic, could you guide us as where to find the relevant portion in the expert report? There are so many pages that you'll understand that I have sometimes some -- need some guidance to find the relevant pages on which you are questioning the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's footnote 119, and in English page 61.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First, we should see this video from 3 minutes, 12 seconds up to 4 minutes, 23 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "I will mark this spot with an X with yellow paint with the number 1 beside it."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Subotic, what did Mr. Fazlic show us in this sequence?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic showed us the place where, to the best of his knowledge, was the second goal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us look at the sequence from 17 minutes, 46 seconds to 19 minutes, 16 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "I will mark this spot with an X with yellow paint with the number 1 beside it."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Now we've seen it from a different angle. And Mr. Barry Hogan marked the point that you've already indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now play the video from 1 minute, 55 seconds to 2 minutes, 55 seconds. Could we now start playing?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Could you please show me, by standing in the spot, where one of the posts for the goal-posts was located on the 1st of June, 1993, please? "Could you now please show me, by standing on the spot, where the second goal-post at this end of the parking-lot was located on the 1st of June, 1993, to the best of your recollection?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did he show us and why is this footage important?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic indicated the range of the goal-posts to the best of his knowledge and their location. He made four steps and we can conclude that the distance between goal-posts was about 4 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could we look at the sequence from 9 minutes, 1 second to 10 minutes 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for that, Mr. Lukic, I had difficulties in finding on page 61 footnote 119. If you could give me a better source than ... I'm looking at the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in English 61.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's 51, yes, but there -- do I find there material which is related to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On -- do you mean e-court page 61 or do you mean page 61 as --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should be same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at the PDF report at this moment, but perhaps I should move to the ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So beginning with 9 minutes, 1 second to 10 minutes, 33 seconds. Let us play this part of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Mr. Fazlic, could you now please show me, by standing on the spot and indicating with your hand, the outer limit of the playing field which was lined with wrecked cars, to the best of your recollection, on the 1st of June, 1993? "Once again, could you please stand on the -- on the spot, and indicate with your hand as you stand on the spot? "I will now draw a line along this plane with yellow spray paint. "Would you now please show me, by standing on the spot, where, to the best of your" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did he show us and why is it important?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic showed us the location of old cars that were lined on the edge -- along the edge of the playing field on the critical location, and it's important because the television filmed on the very same day the footage we indicated in paragraph 35, picture 28, where these cars are at an angle of 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we return to 1D5498.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before moving on to another exhibit, is counsel tendering the video that we've just watched?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that we agreed to tender documents at the end. You proposed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't recall proposing that, but I do think it's more efficient to tender it because we are going to be using a lot of documents to tender as we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most important is that we keep track of it, and one of the advantages of tendering them right away, unless there is any good reason to expect that there would be additions to it, is that we -- once they are tendered, of course we are -- we feel free -- if we have admitted it, we feel free to consult it on our computers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am not sure if this is not in evidence already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you. It's indicated by its 65 -- well, it's by ERN number in footnote 119. So you should tell me whether it's in evidence already, Mr. Lukic. I can't know that. Because it has no P number is -- I think I do remember that I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there has been a still from the video portion that you've seen that's been shown before, if the image is familiar. However, the video itself is not in evidence. We would ask that the full portion from scheduled incident G-4 be included as -- and tendered as a video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not sure if that's what's completely in this clip, but that's what we would ask to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could you upload the G-4 section of that video and then in its entirety so that we have the full context.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would you already that we provide a provisional number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we cannot upload before we get from the Prosecution what they want to have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole of G-4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that's what Mr. Weber asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It's a bit hard, and I'm not [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would you be willing to select the times for the whole of G-4 and then provide that to Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so that he can upload it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will provide the specific time codes, both start and -- and for the ERN so Mr. Lukic can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, Mr. Weber will assist you in getting it into evidence, the whole of G-4. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, yes, we already reserve a number for that. We can't MFI it yet because it's not ... Madam Registrar, the number reserved for the G-4 portion of this video would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1244, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that one is reserved. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness -- Mr. Lukic, there should be no speaking at audible level for -- even when you consult with Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And during this consultation, the microphone should be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I keep forgetting today the whole day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do it now and then as well, Mr. Lukic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, we have already seen your report on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we need picture 28. That's page 64 in B/C/S. And also 64 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did this photograph find its way into your report?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: As you can see, this is a still from a TV broadcast that day. It's a still taken from a film, and it's there for the reasons explained before. We have shown -- in fact, Mr. Fazlic showed the direction --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, I want to ask something now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Namely that the photograph be enlarged and that we see only one photograph on the screen. Now I would like to ask the usher's assistance in helping Ms. Subotic mark certain things here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, could you please mark the place where Mr. Fazlic showed one goal was located?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this circle?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it's really visible here. I have a better photograph in my paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can be seen in this circle?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: One goal that is used in football games. And it's between the red car and the blue car.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Put number 1 there, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness please tell us exactly where she sees a goal in this picture? Because that's, I think, what she said. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look carefully, you will be able to see that between the red car and the blue car, in front of the red car and closer to the red car. Do you want me to draw a line where I see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we first zoom in -- perhaps we get this one, because if you zoom it in then --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need this -- this -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please mark where you see the goal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if you can check picture 29, Your Honour, it's better visible, the small goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the witness has marked where she saw the goal. Do you want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, your microphone is on. One second, please. So you indicated where Mr. Fazlic showed that one of the goals was located. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you tender this marked photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I need something else to be marked on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll wait for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you now please mark, if you can, the place where Mr. Fazlic showed the cars were lined?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You put number 2 there?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you now indicate where the pitch was at Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've written number 3 to mark the pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we take that break, what did you exactly mean by "the pitch," and how did the witness understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was a playing ground, actually, nearby, where football could be played, and it was empty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, you can play wherever football -- wherever you want to play football. But I would have one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the witness to confirm that this was her understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you understand "the pitch" to be what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The playing field. The pitch is a place where football is played. And based on the data and the dimensions showed by Mr. Fazlic, it's perfectly clear that the so-called small football was played then, because the distance, as he showed it, between the goal-posts was 3 metres. It was not big football. The goal-posts were here, where indicated, and they were later removed and instead basketball hoops were placed there. What we marked down below is -- that's the goal-post used for small football.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I do not fully understand what you mean. You marked what you said was a goal between the red and the blue car. Is that a goal that was used during the play as far as you concluded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That was not the goal that was used. Now, all your conclusions, that's all based on analysing documentary evidence, is that well understood? Or has it got anything to do with your expertise as an expert in weaponry and projectiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said at the beginning that in all our reports we wrote what we wrote based on the entire material we had, and they were later grounded and confirmed based on physical evidence, which is the only relevant evidence as far as my profession is concerned. We took into account everything that constituted physical evidence in my profession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not really an answer to my question, because interpreting evidence, whether physical or not -- I mean, to see what a goal is and what the FIFA says what the size of a goal should be, et cetera, that's not within your expertise, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not my area of expertise, but it had to be analysed because there were discrepancies between the indications given by Witness Fazlic and what the television filmed on the scene and what he himself said. We had to find out what it was about, because he was one of the key witnesses in this story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question to you, Ms. Subotic. You said you used physical evidence. What kind of physical evidence did you use to establish that the spot you indicated as number 3 is the playground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, we only used the video footage and the testimony filmed by Mr. Barry Hogan to compare the area where it happened. And as you can see on this picture, we see the trace of one shell. We don't know when it fell. We have traces that are symbolic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- in comparison with a number of victims mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. You said you analysed the evidence of Barry Hogan and the witness to establish that number 3 is the playground, if I understood you correctly. You have no so-called physical evidence with respect to number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- what did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only have the testimony of Mr. -- bear with me for a second, Dinko, who testified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that the shells landed on the playing field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is your interpretation of a witness's evidence. It's what we have in court. You said: "As you can see on this picture, we see the trace of one shell." Where do we find that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You marked the spot with number 4. How did you establish from this footage that this is a trace of a shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not only based on this footage. There were also witness statements that a shell fell on the playing field the previous day, and then we confirmed it based on this still -- just a moment, excuse me. Could you -- could you erase this for me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, we can't move it in any way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you help me, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can't move it at this moment because you're --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Witness, because there are markings on it and then we cannot at this moment change it. What -- what did you want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What did you want to mark?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I wanted to mark blood-stains. It's all much better visible on my enlarged picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now, you crossed out the previous marking number 4 and you put a new marking with number 4 and you say this is -- and you say these are blood --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- stains.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are these blood-stains or a trace of a shell? What is it, blood-stains or trace of a shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. The trace of a shell is in the centre of this number 4, and blood-stains is this stripe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that you now put a number 5 where you consider to be a trace of a shell; is that correct? Or is it blood-stains?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Number 5 are the blood-stains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I try --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, without doing any additional markings, I just want to understand what you did. I asked you where we can see the trace of a shell, and you indicated that you concluded it from witness testimony. You couldn't see that in this picture; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this photograph, we see the trace of an old shell impact that we also have witness testimony about, and the number of people injured --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- during this playing field incident, which was minimal, we concluded that it didn't happen in this place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You are not answering my question. So you may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please -- we take a break, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's better to finish this. Just a couple of more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, fine if you would. But then, of course, we are coming close to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, if you would continue for another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 20 minutes, then, of course we would conclude for the day and have an early -- but I don't know whether Mr. Mladic would prefer to continue for another 20 minutes or take a break first?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My suggestion is not well received, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, it's -- no, we have short sessions. We'll take a break and we'll -- Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before the break, if we could just --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- admit the marked video -- the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, if possible maybe to erase this criss-crossed number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. No, no, we are not going to erase any evidence. Whether it will be adjusted later, you can tender or you cannot tender it. If you do so, we'll -- and then of course, you can have it on the screen back later and do whatever other markings, but the transcript will be incomprehensible if we now would change it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. We tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The marked photo on page 64 of document 1D5498 receives Exhibit D1245, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. The witness may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 5 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Lukic, I would have one question. Witness, you told us that the imprint of a shell impact on the parking-lot was of a previous day. How were you able to establish on what day that imprint was created by the explosion of a shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witnesses stated so. If you want to be able to see the imprint better, it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- is in paragraph 40, image 33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not -- perhaps I may look at it because if your report will be in evidence, we look at every single detail of it. But I just wondered -- so you say that that's an old imprint, that is, a couple of days before, that's because the witnesses said so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And they commented on this picture when saying that this is an old imprint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They stated that a shell had landed on the parking-lot the previous day. They did not comment this still. It comes from the TV footage, which was shown only after the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there also witnesses who said that a shell landed on the parking-lot on the day of the incident at -- that, as a matter of fact, being the incident, are witnesses saying that as well? Other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Other witnesses stated that the game was played on the pitch and the lot. It differed. They only talked about the mines, the shells, which landed at the place where the game was played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And some of them said that that was on the parking-lot, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Fazlic stated that it was in the parking-lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, some stated that it took place in the parking-lot, but I am unable to quote off-the-cuff. If you wish me to do so, I can make a list of who said what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm just wondering what made you choose the one statement to be reliable, the other one not to be reliable. That's -- if witnesses say that they played on the parking-lot and that's where the shell fell, and if you are telling us that the play was somewhere else, then I wonder what makes you -- what brings you in a position to assess the reliability and the accuracy of what those witnesses said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment ago, I responded to another Judge's question. We looked at the footage, and had these imprints been created on that day, with so many people wounded, the footage taken by the TV crew must have shown at least two different imprints and a lot of picture all over the place -- a lot of blood all over the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, when marking the still of this picture, you initially marked a number 4 which you then crossed out again and said that was an imprint of a shell and then you say, no, it was not, and then you marked another place again with 4 which you say was an imprint of a shell. It's -- I'm puzzled by the fact that you say there should have been blood and two imprints because, on the basis of your marking, there is at least one imprint, and initially you said there was another one but you withdrew that, and you said there were blood-stains on the parking-lot. Again, it seems that you explain it by saying that was all from the day before, but it's not entirely clear to me on what basis, having heard your explanation, you drew that conclusion. Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the still was taken on the same day when the incident took place. I also said that Mr. Fazlic and Mr. Dinko stated that a shell had landed the previous day in the parking-lot. I also said that if there were 101 wounded, if the imprints were related to the incident, there would have been far more blood than can be seen in the parking-lot. There is another reason to believe that there was no game played in the parking-lot, which is the small goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I was not inviting you -- I only asked you about what made you believe that the imprints were from the previous day. I now have understood that you have evaluated all the evidence that was available to you, and you concluded that this is how it should have been, including the amount of blood on the floor, et cetera, which all is not within your expertise, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't say so. I cannot look into imprints and traces in an isolated fashion without trying to include them in the overall picture, because then it would put us in the following situation: We have no police report, we do have an UNPROFOR report, and so on. That would be strictly speaking within my domain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it is for this Chamber to evaluate and assess all the evidence which is before it. It's your task to answer questions related to your expertise. And, Mr. Lukic, you are invited to proceed, but could you please try to focus on what this witness can tell us as an expert rather than to draw conclusions on what should have been seen and -- which is totally unrelated to her expertise. Of course, whatever other way you want to establish that, but let's avoid that this witness is doing the job of the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we -- our position is that it is very harmful for the truth to have partial evidence, and that's what is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- happening all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I am not telling you that you should not present other evidence. I am telling you that if you call a witness as an expert on ballistics, that that witness to draw all other kind of conclusions which are to be drawn by the Chamber, present the facts and leave the conclusions in the field of ballistics to the expert and in other fields to the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be possible -- no, no, I have to respond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It would be possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please proceed. Next question to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It would be possible if they were on the site at that time. They had to use everything that they had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I told you - that's my ruling - that you should put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Subotic, you said you did not have a police report from 1993. When was the first police report on the incident created?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: The first one was made in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the basis of their work two years later?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: That is the right question to ask. I'd rather not go into it. In their findings, they state that they found a crater, analysed it, and determined the direction wrongly, inaccurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think there is some confusion. Did you visit the site?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask, when you said they determined the direction wrongly, is that what they said or is that what you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is what I'm telling you based on material evidence and traces found in the parking-lot where they too took their measurements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, did you measure the traces in the single imprint of an exploded shell in the parking-lot?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So your conclusions are based not only on the footage, witness statements, and police reports, but they also included your measurements of a crater in the location where one shell exploded in the parking-lot?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I know we're pressing for the finish today, but can we have some clear record when -- when were these measurements, how were they taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would assist if you would explore that matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry that I missed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- otherwise Mr. Weber will do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, I was cautioned to verify English interpretation. What you found, is it one of two traces or the only one?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: In 1995, it was the only trace, as we were able to establish when examining a witness who was in charge of the investigation when he testified in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Would the witness kindly repeat the last name because we did not hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you find the other one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Lukic. Witness, could you repeat the name of that witness? The last name you mentioned, because the interpreters couldn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Mirza Sabljica, the gentleman who was in charge of the investigation. He is a ballistics expert of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you gave the name. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, did you manage to locate the other imprint?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: In 2010 when we visited the location, there were two imprints in the parking-lot. They can also be found in the documents -- recorded in the documents created back in 2001 by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to the documents you were able to review, when is the first mention of the second imprint?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC
utterances.text: We found it for the first time in 2001, meaning that it occurred sometime in between, between 1995 and 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's the end of our workday, at least in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I would have one short question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said in 1995 there was only one trace, and you learned that from a witness. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I said that I read it in the CSB report, which conducted its first investigation relating to the incident at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps you could -- could you tell us which report that exactly was and where it is footnoted, perhaps? Is that what we find on page -- is that Exhibit P872?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, footnote 148 and several others, because we've referred to it multiple times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 148. That's P872. Thank you for that information. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And only when Mirza Sabljica testified and where. Maybe this witness should clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, couldn't the parties agree on where he testified and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our position is that he testified during the trial in Karadzic case and he gave that -- that data --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But again, was the witness there when he testified? This witness was there? But you both are aware of when he testified in the Karadzic case, isn't it? Is that something -- is there any dispute about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no dispute on our side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- that he testified that there was only one marking when he was conducting the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the content of the testimony --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which is different from whether he testified or not. Apparently the parties agree that he testified and we'll hear any further details if need be tomorrow. Witness, I -- we'll adjourn for the day. We would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. As I instructed you before, you're not allowed to speak or communicate by whatever means with whomever, that includes counsel, that includes co-authors of your report, about your testimony. If that's clear to you, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning and you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I again urge you to focus on what such a witness could bring us; that is, that she tells us about her expertise, that she does not start to evaluate the totality of the evidence. We not even knowing exactly always what it is that she has seen or what she has not seen. But if she moves away from her expertise, she should be considered a witness of fact and then we need a clear foundation of the sources of knowledge. And as usual, witnesses of fact are not expected to give an evaluation of the evidence. We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 23rd of September, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd day of September, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.17 p.m.,
